source.title: Improving Generalization via Uncertainty Driven Perturbations
source.authors: Matteo Pagliardini; Gilberto Manunza; Martin Jaggi; Michael I. Jordan; Tatjana Chavdarova

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figures are represented only by captions or plots.
record.tranche_reason: Tests a new uncertainty-driven perturbation training method on image datasets and reports clean test accuracy, robustness and feature-transfer results related to generalization.
record.gate_note: The paper reports UDP results against clean-training, PGD and TRADES baselines. Prior-work results cited in the paper are not recorded as rows. Figure-only capacity and accuracy sweeps are omitted where the text gives no extractable values.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates uncertainty-driven perturbation training, robustness, transfer accuracy and low-data accuracy. None of its results tests V1–V8. Its width sweep does not establish zero training error or generalization beyond the interpolation threshold; its dropout experiment does not isolate dropout's effect on test error.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose uncertainty-driven perturbations to improve classification margins, interpret transfer results as reduced simplicity bias, and report competitive robustness–accuracy trade-offs and improved low-data accuracy. They describe their real-world experiments as preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces uncertainty-driven input or latent-space perturbations during training, evaluated mainly against PGD and TRADES perturbation training; it is not a reproduction of the claim's natural-label generalization experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Perturbation magnitude ϵtrain; input versus latent space; dataset; model capacity; augmentation; perturbation method. UDP often selects larger ϵtrain, with results varying across datasets and robustness measures.

fits_no_version.finding: UDP achieves competitive, sometimes improved, robustness–clean-accuracy trade-offs against PGD and TRADES. Latent-space UDPR reaches 53.1 ± 0.9 clean accuracy versus 48.2 ± 0.9 for clean training with 5% of CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Uncertainty-driven perturbation training can improve robustness–accuracy trade-offs and low-data clean accuracy in some image-classification settings.

fits_no_version.finding: UDP-trained CIFAR-10 features achieve 45.3 ± 0.3 CIFAR-100 transfer accuracy, versus 42.5 ± 0.3 for the baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: UDP training can improve fixed-feature transfer from CIFAR-10 to CIFAR-100.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report that wider UDP-trained LeNet models exceed the capacity-1 clean-training baseline on Fashion-MNIST; interpolation and training-error measurements are absent.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing capacity can improve UDP clean accuracy enough to exceed a smaller clean-trained model in the tested setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Single-step UDP-PGD shows a smaller decline in PGD-20 robustness than FGSM training on Fashion-MNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Single-step UDP training can mitigate catastrophic overfitting relative to FGSM in the tested setting.

record.problems: Some clean-accuracy comparisons and the capacity sweep are figure-only with no exact values in the text. The paper describes its empirical results as preliminary and does not report random-label memorization or training-test gaps.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for further individual robustness metrics and conditions in Tables 1–3 are omitted to keep the catalog focused on findings related to clean accuracy/generalization and within the row limit. Figure-only accuracy curves in Figures 4 and 12 lack exact values; only the textual qualitative comparison is summarized in R1–R2. Figure 14's CIFAR-10 catastrophic-overfitting curves have no descriptive numerical values, so they are not separately rowed.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization; held-out chance accuracy under random labels.
Test error after widening beyond the width required for zero training error. The UDP capacity sweep does not locate this threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity, learned sparsity and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization under controlled tuning, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipes that mitigate large-batch penalties.
Dropout's effect on held-out error, including small-data and excessive-dropout regimes. MC dropout supplies uncertainty estimates without a controlled dropout comparison.
Magnitude-scaled weight sharpness versus training–test gaps and its ranking against other measures. Input-space margins and robustness do not test this relation.
Identifying memorized examples, removing them and comparing retrained accuracy with random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain linked to none. Their cannot_determine states concern V1–V8, not whether the reported method improvements occurred. These method-performance results should remain outside the evidence rows for those versions.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or held-out random-label accuracy comparison.
The capacity sweep uses UDP on Fashion-MNIST; it does not establish the width needed for zero training error or test error across the interpolation threshold.
No matched comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks trained from scratch.
No adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparison; optimizer results are not isolated.
Dropout is used for MC-dropout uncertainty estimation in an appendix experiment, but its regularization effect is not compared.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other measure of the training-test gap is tested.
No memorized training examples are identified, removed or retrained.
